page: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz, the instance exposes 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading. It features 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache and hardware extensions including AVX-512, AMX, and cryptographic acceleration instructions.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside constrained parallel execution. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a strong single-core score of 2090.0 and robust text processing performance of 2508.0. Multi-core performance is constrained by the 4-vCPU count, scoring 4757.0 in Geekbench multi-core and registering in the lower percentile on stress-ng multi-core and Clang software compilation benchmarks. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks reached 35.14 GB/sec for reads and 24.76 GB/sec for writes.

The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached remote storage configurations supported by its Premium Storage design. The constrained vCPU layout optimizes software licensing costs that scale by core count while retaining a full 64.0 GB memory footprint.

This hardware profile is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that require large RAM allocations but do not demand high multi-threaded compute density. Key workload fits include enterprise relational databases, in-memory caches, middleware, and memory-bound analytics engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked up to 4.2 GHz. Designed with a constrained core configuration on Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 16.0 GB of memory per core and 260 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector extensions like AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2090.0, while multi-core metrics reflect the restricted 4-vCPU count. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, directing I/O to remote storage. By packaging a large memory pool with reduced core counts, it provides a cost-effective operational profile for core-licensed relational database workloads, in-memory processing, and caching systems.
